cohort: A total of 218 pregnant women from the Obstetrics Department of the Second Affiliated Hospital of Guilin Medical College from August 2016 to August 2017 were enrolled and divided into a control group (n=107, <5 prenatal examinations) and a research group (n=111, >=5 prenatal examinations).
finding: Higher compliance with prenatal examinations (>=5 times) was associated with significantly lower incidence rates of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including cesarean section, placental abruption, premature birth, prolonged pregnancy, pregnancy-induced hypertension, placenta previa, and postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: The incidence of cesarean section was significantly lower in the group with higher prenatal examination compliance.
